newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to give more powers to central bank.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to give more powers to central bank.

text.p: The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) said on Thursday it would be granted greater powers to regulate the banking system and control monetary policy.
An SBP statement said the caretaker government would issue ordinances soon to amend the State Bank of Pakistan Act, Banks Nationalisation Act and Banking Companies Ordinance.
"These changes give extensive powers to the State Bank for regulation of the banking system," it quoted central bank governor Mohammad Yaqub as telling bankers on Wednesday.
"The autonomy of the State Bank in formulation and implementation of monetary policy has also been substantially enhanced," Yaqub said.
He said the changes would enable the SBP Board of Directors to conduct monetary policy independently, and to determine and regulate money supply and government borrowing from the SBP.
Yaqub said the central bank's regulatory power had been strengthened by increasing ten-fold the penalties banks must pay for various violations.

He said the government was also formulating new laws on foreclosure and banking tribunals to speed up the process of recovery of bad debts; the merger and consolidation of various state-run financial institutions; and setting up a Resolution Trust Corporation to dispose of their non-performing portfolios.
Yaqub asked banks and financial institutions to submit to the central bank within a month their policies on lending, writing off and rescheduling of loans.
